facts.F26: OQ3 Clients: the wire gains one metric key arrivals whose sides carry the members total, perDay, throughputPerDay and gapPerDay (each a CapturedValue, doubles unrounded). lighthouse-clients holds no list of report metric keys or members (packages/client reportWording.ts and mcp-core reportTools.ts pass the raw answer through, per ADR-247), so no client code or release is needed. Only the lighthouse-reports skill reference (separate repo, prose) must learn the gap wording, the lower-is-better direction, and that Then is never rebuilt; the skill evals and drift test there own it. No changeset.
facts.F27: OQ5 Wording: started and finished are fixed English words, not terminology tokens (Arrivals is a fixed name too: the Metrics tab uses the literal word and the seeder has no Arrivals key; a new key would need seeding for no reader gain). The tokens {Work Item}/{Work Items} (total line, as ThroughputPanel) and {Throughput} (line title) stay tokens. Rows: Total started N {Work Items}; Arrivals per day X.XX per day; {Throughput} per day X.XX per day; gap line. Gap line copy from the rounded gap g: g>0 -> g.toFixed(2) more started than finished per day; g<0 -> |g|.toFixed(2) fewer started than finished per day; g==0 -> as many started as finished per day. Number is never signed with a plus or minus on the Then and Now sides; the words carry the sign. Singular/plural: none needed, the sentence uses the unit per day, and the total line reuses the {Work Item}/{Work Items} choice of ThroughputPanel.
facts.F28: Rounding: PER_DAY_DECIMALS = 2 (ThroughputPanel). The backend freezes gapPerDay = arrivalsPerDay - throughputPerDay from the unrounded per-day values of one pair of series; the frontend rounds each side with roundForDisplay(.,2), and M10 balanced iff the rounded gap is 0 (so 0.004 reads balanced, 0.006 reads 0.01 more). The change line is compareThenNow on the SHOWN gaps (lineComparisonsOf already rounds both sides before subtracting), so shown Then + shown change = shown Now, the ADR-220 rule; 0.30 and -0.10 give -0.40 better. Rejected: change from unrounded values, because the displayed numbers could then contradict the displayed change.
facts.F29: Gap owner: the arithmetic arrivals minus throughput lives once, in the new backend ArrivalsReportMetric (cohesive owner, a WindowedReportMetric beside ThroughputReportMetric), so Then and Now use one computation and the clients receive the gap raw. The frontend ArrivalsPanel owns only presentation: rounding, the three sentences, the mark. Direction of good (lower) lives only in reportPanelRegistry (ADR-220). No domain decision sits in a React component beyond the wording of an already computed value.
facts.F3: When creating a Then & Now report for a Team or a Portfolio, the reader can tick Arrivals; the report then shows an Arrivals panel that, for Then and for Now, gives the Work Items started in total and per day, Throughput per day, and the gap per day (started minus finished) in words with its sign, with a change mark on the gap where a lower gap is better and no percent change.
facts.F30: Old reports (M6, Epic 5878 D27, followed as is): Read leaves out members the report never froze, so an old report has no arrivals metric and ReportPanels draws NOTHING_CAPTURED; the panel shows dashes and the existing absence note Not captured for this report on both sides. The edit wizard already lists a metric whose key is missing from the captured keys as a disabled, unticked checkbox with the helper Not captured for this report, and ThenAndNowTemplate.Edit refuses MetricNotCaptured for it; no new code. An old report cannot show Arrivals at all (shown keys are only ever from the stored list), so the panel appears only if a user had ticked it, which is impossible; the not captured read stays as the defensive look. New reports capture arrivals for every owner, shown or not, like the other metrics.
facts.F31: Header summary: the registry entry has one change line, gapPerDay, with changeLines [gapPerDay, label gap per day, decimals 2], so summariseChange needs no change: gap change below zero lists Arrivals under Improved, above zero under Got worse, shown change zero under Unchanged, and a dash on either side (not captured) puts it in no group, as for other metrics. The group name is the panel title Arrivals.
facts.F32: Edge cases: nothing finished gives throughput total 0 and perDay 0.00 as a real value (the Throughput rule; no absentReason), so gap = arrivals per day. Nothing started gives arrivals 0 and 0.00 and gap = -throughput per day (fewer started), or zero (as many started as finished) if nothing finished. Window days come from the series length, as Throughput, so no division by zero for a window of at least one day. Absent members use the existing CapturedValue.Absent plus absenceTextOf. Windows inside the done-items cutoff: Then creation is already refused by ReportWindowPolicy.ThenRefusal; Now uses the same series. Portfolio arrivals are Features started: PortfolioReportMetricSeries reads IPortfolioMetricsService.GetArrivalsForPortfolio (the Metrics tab's own reader), Team reads ITeamMetricsService.GetStartedItemsForTeam (the Metrics tab's arrivals endpoint). One definition of arrival; BuildArrivalsInfoDto is not reused because it computes a previous-period comparison, a different shape.
facts.F33: Throughput repeated: throughputPerDay is stored inside the arrivals capture from the same IReportMetricSeries.DailyThroughput the Throughput metric reads over the same window and day count, so both panels show the same number: Then is frozen in one CaptureThen call per metric at one instant over the same series and Now is computed from the same Metrics tab reader on each read. Stored twice by design (the panel must read alone and a report may hide Throughput); never disagree because both come from one reader and one window. The change mark of Throughput never depends on it.
facts.F34: Loading and failure looks: no new fetch. No separate loading or failure look exists for the panel. The panel also reads a dash with the reason in the Not captured and no-finished states.

facts.F38: Cross-layer algebra. Domain (Reports metric): state = per-window CapturedValue members {total, perDay, throughputPerDay, gapPerDay} with total integer and gapPerDay = perDay - throughputPerDay; operations CaptureThen/Read over a window; observation = the four values per side; equality = field-wise CapturedValue equality. Application/port: IReportMetricSeries gains DailyArrivals(owner, window) returning one count per day; outcome is values or ReportOwnerGoneException like the other series. Adapter: TeamReportMetricSeries/PortfolioReportMetricSeries map the Metrics services' RunChartData to counts through DailyCounts (the order and the day count are the window's). Presentation: ArrivalsPanel maps four values to rows plus one gap sentence; absent values map to dash and note. Infrastructure/recovery: none new; the Then payload is the existing JSON column captures, a new key in the existing JsonObject, no migration (EF migrations N/A); old payloads lack the key and read as not captured.
facts.F40: Checker mapping: no state machine, concurrency or liveness is introduced, so Quint (installed, 0.33.1) and TLC/Agda are not applicable; the claims are total pure arithmetic on two numbers and a sign-word mapping, falsified by native properties: fast-check (frontend package.json, fast-check 4.10.2) for the rounding and sign-word laws, and NUnit TestCase rows for the backend capture (no FsCheck in the backend manifest). Type strength: the C# CapturedValue record and the TS union of sentence kinds; invalid states (a plus-signed zero, '0.00 more') are excluded by a three-way closed sum returned by gapSentenceOf, but the TS wire type stays a nullable number as for other members. Property tests: see laws.
facts.F41: Prefactoring: none needed on behavior; one small move before the feature, extracting the 'metric name or term key' choice behind metricNameOf in reportPanelRegistry is part of the feature itself, not a preserving move. No smell blocks the new metric: code-fact (code-fact query.callers-of) was not run; readings were by hand with ctx_shell/grep, which is noisy and could miss dynamic callers, so a consumer of ReportMetricSide keys outside the grepped Reports tree is unknown.
